mentions.name: LACE
mentions.description: A self-organising research companion for long-horizon inquiry. It captures fragments from the web via a browser extension, auto-clusters them into evolving "threads" and projects with summaries and reading lists, maintains a graph of connections across threads ("topology of attention"), and turns a cluster of fragments into an essay draft when ready to share. Built as a web app with an LLM pipeline, using neo4j's llm-graph-builder as a starting point; currently in a small test phase.
mentions.problem: With LLMs, generating ideas and snippets is cheap, but keeping track of fragments with their "why I cared" context over months is hard. Most tools like Notion or Obsidian assume the user will do the work of maintaining folder/tag/linking structure forever.
mentions.audience: Researchers, writers, engineers, and founders who constantly lose good ideas in their notes
